oauth.alternatives: LinkedIn has no open API for reading messages, feed, connections or other members' profiles. Those need partner programs (Sales Navigator, Talent, Marketing). Compliance is closed. If your agent needs inbox or network data, a normal app cannot get it.

appTypes.name: Developer app (3-legged member auth)
appTypes.whenToUse: Use for an agent product where each user connects their own LinkedIn account. One app serves all users. The products you add decide the scopes.

appTypes.name: Application auth (2-legged client credentials)
appTypes.whenToUse: Only for partner programs that need app-level data. Not for member accounts.

verdict.label: Self-serve, optional review
verdict.summary: Any LinkedIn member can connect to your own app through the self-serve products (Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect, Share on LinkedIn) with no review. Reading anything beyond the member's own basic profile needs partner approval that LinkedIn may refuse, which is tier 5 for those use cases.
verdict.nextStep: Create an app at https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps and add the two self-serve products on the Products tab.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Members consent for themselves. No org admin approval step appeared in the docs I read.

composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth app for LinkedIn, so you can start today. Moving to your own app later only affects new connections. Existing users must reconnect.

stages.name: Prototype
stages.whoCanConnect: Anyone with a LinkedIn account can authorize once the self-serve products are enabled. No test-user list was documented.
stages.notes: App creation may require linking a LinkedIn Page. Not confirmed.

stages.name: Production (self-serve scopes)
stages.whoCanConnect: Any member, using openid, profile, email, w_member_social.
stages.notes: Extra products (Advertising API, Sales Navigator, Talent) need LinkedIn approval with no stated timeline.

scopeTiers.name: Open permissions
scopeTiers.effect: Self-serve on the Products tab. Gives the member's own name, headline, photo, email, and posting, commenting and liking for them.

scopeTiers.name: Marketing (Advertising API)
scopeTiers.effect: You must apply and be approved through the Products tab.

scopeTiers.name: Sales and Talent partner programs
scopeTiers.effect: Needs approval as a partner. It can be refused.

requirements.detail: Sign in and create an app in the developer portal. You need an app name and logo, and possibly a LinkedIn Page (unconfirmed).
Add absolute HTTPS callback URLs on the Auth tab. No fragments. Query parameters are ignored.
Add Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn on the Products tab.
Your logo and app name show on the consent screen. Publish a privacy policy before launch. This is good practice; a LinkedIn requirement was not confirmed.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Open the developer portal, click Create app, fill in name, logo and Page, and accept the terms.

steps.title: Enable products
steps.detail: On the app's Products tab, request Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn. Both are self-serve.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs
steps.detail: On the Auth tab, add exact absolute HTTPS callback URLs. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Implement the code flow
steps.detail: Send users to https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization with response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state and scope. Exchange the code at /oauth/v2/accessToken within 30 minutes.

steps.title: Plan for token expiry
steps.detail: Access tokens last 60 days. Programmatic refresh tokens are only for some partners, so plan to send users through the authorize flow again before expiry.

steps.title: Set branding
steps.detail: Under My apps > Settings, set the logo and name shown on the consent screen.

steps.title: Decide on extra access
steps.detail: If you need ads, sales or talent data, apply on the Products tab or the partner program page. The outcome is uncertain and no timeline is stated.

steps.title: Move off Composio managed app
steps.detail: Switch your auth config to your own client ID. Existing users must reconnect.

blockers.cause: The redirect URL differs from the one on the Auth tab.
blockers.fix: Register the exact URL and send the same value in the authorize and token requests.

blockers.cause: The scope is not granted to the app because the product is not enabled.
blockers.fix: Add the matching product on the Products tab, then check the Auth tab for scopes.

blockers.symptom: Users must consent again about every 60 days
blockers.cause: Access tokens last 60 days and refresh tokens are partner-only.
blockers.fix: Re-run the authorize flow before expiry. It skips the screen if the member is still logged in and the token is valid.

blockers.symptom: You need messages, connections or feed and no scope exists
blockers.cause: Open permissions only cover the member's own profile, email and posting.
blockers.fix: Apply to the relevant partner program or drop the feature.
blockers.escalation: Submit a developer support request from the LinkedIn developer portal.

blockers.symptom: Earlier tokens stop working after you change scopes
blockers.cause: Requesting a different scope invalidates earlier tokens.
blockers.fix: Ask for the full scope set up front. Users must re-authenticate after scope changes.

We request only openid, profile, email and w_member_social. We never post without the user's confirmation. Users can disconnect at any time.

evidence.claim: LinkedIn uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow. HTTPS redirect URLs must match exactly. Codes last 30 minutes. Access tokens last 60 days. Programmatic refresh is for limited partners. Scope changes force re-consent.
Open permissions (profile, email, w_member_social) are self-serve. Most other permissions and partner programs need approval. Compliance is closed.
No OIDC discovery document at linkedin.com; the authorize endpoint is live.
evidence.note: Authorization endpoint live and rejects an unknown client ID. Discovery document returned 404.

evidence.claim: Tier 2 for self-serve scopes, tier 5 for anything else.
evidence.note: From e2: open permissions need no approval; other permissions need approval that may be refused.
